title: Resilient routing: automatic fallback triggers & per-route circuit breakers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement automatic fallback triggers and circuit breaker behavior for smart routing. Scope: region selection, tier routing (hosted/dedicated/private), and model-variant fallbacks. Goal is to ensure predictable degradation (fast, low-cost fallbacks) when a route, region, or model variant exceeds error/latency thresholds without creating cascading outages.
background: We already have basic autofallback behavior (ENG-7421) but it is coarse-grained and reacts mainly to simple 429s. Customers want more predictable, configurable behavior when facing partial regional outages, overloaded dedicated pools, and bad model variants after rollouts. We need per-route and per-entity circuit breakers with multi-signal triggers (429 rate, 5xx rate, median P95 latency, endpoint timeouts) and safe defaults for PLG customers.
proposal:
Introduce a multi-criteria circuit breaker and fallback system with the following characteristics:
1) Signals: 429 rate, 5xx rate, timeout rate, P95 latency. Each signal contributes to a weighted risk score for the target (route/region/model-variant/pool).
2) Thresholds: default conservative thresholds (e.g., 429>5% over 60s, 5xx>1% over 60s, timeout>0.5% over 60s, P95 latency > 1.5x SLA) with per-customer overrides.
3) Actions: soft-fallback (route to cheaper compatible variant or next tier), hard-circuit-open (quarantine the endpoint for a cooldown window), and retry-with-backoff for transient errors.
4) Scope: breakers tracked at multiple granularities: route+region, model-variant, customer-tier (hosted/dedicated/private), and node-pool.
5) Hysteresis & cooldown: exponential backoff for re-probing, minimum open window defaults, and gradual ramp recovery to avoid oscillation.
6) Observability: expose per-breaker metric streams, reason codes, and last-triggered state to Console and APIs.
7) Safety: rate-limited global fallback to prevent mass failover on control-plane issues.
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Architecture review with Runtime and Platform teams. Agreed to weight signals and track score instead of single-signal gating (avoids false positives). 2026-03-11: PM approved default thresholds and per-customer overrides. Design signed off by SRE (Morgan Rivera) pending implementation of monitoring dashboards.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement per-route scoring engine in routing service, simple in-memory breaker states, and soft-fallback to model-variant list. Phase 2 (2-3 weeks): persistent breaker state in config-store, exponential cooldowns, and region-aware policies. Phase 3 (1 week): Console surfaces, metrics, and alerting rules. Phase 4: gradual rollout + canary on low-traffic customers and dedicated pools.
rollout_plan:
- Start with non-critical routes (internal tools) on staging.
- Canary group: 5% of PLG traffic + 2 dedicated customers (coordinated).
- Monitor key metrics for 48 hours (fallback count, successful retries, customer error rate).
- If regressions > defined thresholds, rollback the router rollout only (no model changes).
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic. Integration tests that simulate: sustained 429 bursts, spike in P95 latency, backend timeouts, and mixed-signal degradation. Chaos test: induce partial region network partitions in staging to verify safe failover. Load test with synthetic traffic to ensure breaker evaluation cost is negligible.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: breaker_state{scope,reason}, breaker_score, fallback_actions, fallback_latency_penalty, recovery_attempts. Alerts: >10% of requests experiencing fallback in 5m for a customer (warn), >50% fallback or repeated circuit flaps (SEV2). Dashboards: per-route heatmap and timeline for breaker triggers and recoveries.
acceptance_criteria: Default breaker config prevents large-scale routing cascades in 3 simulated outage scenarios
No more than 1% additional end-to-end error rate for unaffected routes during canary rollout
Metrics and Console panel show breaker state and reason codes for all canary traffic
